newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court jails Hanbo founder for 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court jails Hanbo founder for 15 years.

text.p: A South Korean court on Monday handed a 15-year jail sentence to the founder of the scandal-ridden Hanbo Group, Chung Tae-soo, in a corruption case that has rocked the nation, television reports said.
Chung's son, Hanbo chairman Chung Bo-keun, was handed a three-year jail term. Both were convicted of bribery and embezzlement.

Eight other people, including senior lawmakers, a former cabinet minister and former top bankers were also jailed in connection with a loans-for-kickbacks scandal that emerged after Hanbo's steelmaking flagship folded in January. Hanbo's one-time financial controller was handed a suspended jail term.
Former Home Affairs minister Kim Woo-suk was jailed for four years. Among the politicians, Hong In-gil of the ruling New Korea Party received the heaviest punishment with a seven-year jail sentence.

"Your wrongdoing has caused a great shock to the Korean people, harm to the country's economy and chaos in society," chief judge Son Ji-yol said in sentencing the founder of South Korea's 14th largest business conglomerate.
